messages:
elaine-peopleops: Heads-up Q: how should managers submit a comp regrade vs a promotion? We have a case where role unchanged but market movement suggests a salary increase.

mike-eng: We saw a couple of folks where title stayed same but scope grew. Is that "regrade" or "promo" in the system?

priya-manager: Practically: regrade = same level/title, comp adjustment only. Promotion = level or title change. Which forms do we use?

elaine-peopleops: Good distinction. Use the 'Comp Change' flow for salary-only adjustments (Comp Change form). Use 'Promotion Request' when level/title change is requested. Both routes require manager justification + comp partner review.

mike-eng: What evidence do comp partners want for market-driven regrades?

comp-partner: Short answer: market data + comp rationale. Upload 1) external comp benchmark (source + date), 2) internal comppeers table (3 comps), 3) impact note (2 bullets). We want a one-line headline "Why now" at the top.

priya-manager: Any deadlines to hit payroll for 1st of the month effective dates?

elaine-peopleops: Yes. For salary-only comp changes to be effective on the 1st, packet must be fully approved and in payroll feeds by the 12th prior month. Example: effective 2026-07-01 requires approvals + feeds by 2026-06-12. Promotion packets follow the comp committee timelines (dates posted in People Ops calendar).

payroll-bot: [automated] Payroll feed window: monthly cutoff at 23:59 PT on the 12th. Retro window: 30 days after effective date.

mike-eng: If comp change is approved after cutoff, do we auto-retro or need manual ticket?

comp-partner: We auto-retro within 30-day window — payroll posts an adjustment. If beyond 30 days, request executive exception and submit ticket to payroll@redwood.internal.

priya-manager: For comps that push someone above band top, what docs are required?

elaine-peopleops: Must include two external survey points (source + percentile), business justification (retention/market/critical skill), and VP-level approval. Exceptions flagged in the comp system escalate automatically.

mike-eng: How do we handle leveling panel vs comp committee timing? They sometimes run on different cadences.

comp-partner: Leveling (panel) approves level assignments and can complete independently. Compensation committee approves pay. For a salary change at promotion, both must finish before payroll feeds. If leveling finishes first but comp is pending, level will be updated in org system, salary waits for comp approval.

priya-manager: One edge case: transitioning managers who leave mid-cycle — who signs the packet?

elaine-peopleops: If manager leaves, the skip-level or delegated approver signs. Recruiting or current manager should note the approver in the packet. People Ops will reach out if any signature is missing.

mike-eng: Any template for the one-line headline + 3-bullet justification? Saves time.

elaine-peopleops: Yes, pinned doc: https://redwood.internal/hr/promo-templates. Use format: 1) Headline ("Recommend regrade to $X for market alignment"), 2) Bullet: specific scope change, 3) Bullet: measurable impact, 4) Bullet: evidence/peers. We'll add an example regrade template today.

comp-partner: Tip: if you're asking >15% adjustment, include career-leveling evidence and peer comps to avoid extra review cycles.

priya-manager: Thanks — I'll prep a Comp Change packet and loop comp-partner for early feedback.

payroll-bot: [automated] Reminder: Next comp committee meeting 2026-06-09. Submit packets by 2026-06-01 to be included.
